chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-'Ala' and from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding two men who testified against a man whose wife was absent that he had divorced her, so the woman observed the waiting period and married another; then the absent husband returned and claimed he had not divorced her, and one of the two witnesses proved him false. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The other [witness] has no claim upon her, and the dowry is taken from the one who testified and returned, and it is returned to the latter [husband], and they are separated, and she observes the waiting period from the latter, and the first [husband] does not approach her until her waiting period is completed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the fiqh ruling when an absent husband returns and one of two divorce witnesses is proven false?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the principle of 'kadhīb al-shāhid' (the lying witness) in the context of absent husbands, where the burden of proof shifts to the witnesses. It establishes that the false witness bears the financial penalty by returning the dowry to the second husband, while the first husband must observe the 'iddah of the second marriage before reuniting, ensuring the validity of the intervening union.
